images.title: Spider's shortest path
images.purpose: Show the two box faces laid flat so the spider's path becomes one straight line.
images.composition: One large flat rectangle made of two joined faces, with a single bold diagonal path and generous white space around.
exact_structure: A flat rectangle 6 units wide and 7 units tall made of two stacked faces: the lower face 6 by 4 in light teal (#0072B2) and the upper face 6 by 3 in light amber (#E69F00), joined along a shared grey (#6B7280) fold line.
A bold reddish purple (#CC79A7) straight diagonal from the bottom left corner to the top right corner, labelled about 9.2 cm.
A small dot at the bottom left corner labelled start and a small dot at the top right corner labelled end.
Side labels: 6 cm along the bottom, 4 cm and 3 cm along the right side beside the two faces.
rejection: the rectangle not having a 4 cm face and a 3 cm face stacked against a 6 cm width
the path not being one straight diagonal
images.takeaway: Lay two faces flat and the shortest path across them is a straight line, about 9.2 cm here.
images.description: Two box faces laid flat with a straight diagonal path of about 9.2 cm from start to end.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Notice that the path bends on the box but is straight on the flat picture.

image_decisions.why: The unfolded picture is the method of the whole concept.
